verdict.rationale: Skyvern documents drop-in AI commands on top of Playwright that act on pages through natural language, with selectors as a fallback. It also claims AI is injected into every page interaction and that it maps visual elements to actions on unseen sites, so tests adapt when the UI changes. One hands-on report of failing to click a tab and a popup on a new site lowers confidence but does not concretely refute resilience to selector changes. Missing for 10: detailed per-primitive docs for click/type on described elements, independent corroboration of surviving selector and layout changes.

support.subject: As a developer, I can drive the page through DOM-understanding action primitives (act/click/type on described elements) that survive selector and layout changes

citations.quote: Drop-in AI commands on top of Playwright. Use natural language to act, extract, and validate — or fall back to selectors.
layers Playwright on top, and injects AI into every page interaction
Skyvern can operate on websites it's never seen before, as it's able to map visual elements to actions necessary to complete a workflow, without any customized code
Run end-to-end browser tests that adapt when the UI changes.
